findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Clients schema
findings.body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP v2 before this change therefore retain only the old Users resource/scopes and never receive the Clients resource type, its six scopes, or the all-Clients resource. Client authorization cannot be configured in those realms; moreover `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, ...)` can obtain a null all-Clients resource and pass it to `findByResource`/`ResourcePermission`. Initialize or migrate missing schema scopes/resources even when the admin-permissions client already exists, and add an upgrade-path test.

findings.title: manage-clients administrators lose role-mapping access under v2
findings.body: The overrides for `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` evaluate only a v2 resource permission and omit the normal `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin-role bypass. Consequently, an administrator assigned the standard `manage-clients` role is forbidden from client role mappings, composite role changes, and client-scope role mappings whenever FGAP v2 is enabled, despite retaining that role's established permissions. Preserve the admin-role behavior (and any intended manage transitivity) before evaluating fine-grained scopes.

findings.title: Removal cleanup is disabled when only the v2 feature is enabled
findings.body: The event listener now processes role/client/group removal only when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, but the new implementation is selected by the distinct `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` feature. A deployment enabling v2 without the old feature will skip `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` on removals, leaving associated authorization policies/resources behind for deleted objects. Gate this on v2 as well (or retain the previous unconditional cleanup behavior) so v2-only deployments clean up correctly.
